Count Dooku also trained Vos in some elements of [[Form II/Legends|Form II/Makashi]], while characterizing Vos' dueling skills as "appalling."<ref name="Jedi: Count Dooku" /> The Kiffar had also been shown to hold his lightsaber in reverse grip, indicating he was a practitioner of Form V/Shien. Such examples of this fighting style were displayed in various missions: Anzat,<ref name="darkness" /> Kiffex,<ref name="Rite of Passage" /> Kiffu,<ref name="Jedi: Count Dooku" /> the assassination of Senator Viento,<ref name="Striking from the Shadows" /> ''Titavian IV'',<ref name="Dreadnaughts of Rendili 1" /> Saleucami,<ref name="Siege of Saleucami 1" /> and Kashyyyk.<ref name="The Hidden Enemy 3" /> At one time, he utilized [[Jar'Kai/Legends|Jar'Kai]] against Tysr.<ref name="Rite of Passage" /> Vos's abilities with a lightsaber allowed him to defeat and slay three Dark Acolytes during the Clone Wars; Kadrian Sey,<ref name="Jedi: Count Dooku" /> Tol Skorr, and even Sora Bulq with the support of his fellow Jedi through the Force technique of [[Battle meditation/Legends|battle meditation]].<ref name="The Siege of Saleucami 4" />
[[File:AaylaQuin-wheel.jpg|thumb|250px|Vos using a [[WESTAR-34 blaster pistol/Legends|WESTAR-34 blaster pistol]].]]
In addition to his considerable lightsaber combat skills, Vos had the power of psychometry, the ability to read images from objects. Vos was also one of the few Jedi who was able to use [[Force cloak]], which he learned from Tholme and taught Secura. He could locate his enemies based on their effects on the environment. He also had considerable working knowledge of espionage and counter-intelligence, and worked as a double agent. While working undercover, Dooku personally trained Quinlan Vos in the dark side and in a variety of dark side powers including Force lightning, [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force choke|Force choke]], and to [[Animal bond|tame animals and bend them to his will]], most notably a krayt dragon.<ref name="The Hidden Enemy 3" /> Following his recruitment into Dooku's servce, he tried to learn the Force power [[inertia]], but dislocated his shoulder in the process.<ref name="Book of Sith" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|We had already done some creation of the character and Jan wanted him to be connected to TPM --- which had appeared in the movie theaters by that time. LFL agreed we could use a background character. Jan [spotted] him while watching the movie. She can see a hummingbird flap [its] wing. I'm totally serious about that. >I&lt; didn't spot him until [TPM] was out on DVD and THEN I had to freeze frame to it.|John Ostrander, on how he and Jan Duursema came up with Quinlan Vos's character|<ref name="Ostrander Discussion">{{JCFCite|url=posts/21665687|board=Literature|thread=The Official John Ostrander Discussion Thread|user=[[John Ostrander|jfostrander]]|date=2005-09-22|time=10:05 AM|archivedate=20210516142804}}</ref>}}
[[File:VosAndRags.png|thumb|left|200px|Quinlan Vos's first appearance in ''The Phantom Menace''.]]
Quinlan Vos first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. His appearance in that film was confirmed by his [[Databank (original)|Databank]] and [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|Encyclopedia]] entries, as well as his [[Star Wars: The Vintage Collection]] action figure from 2012.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|quinlanvos|Vos, Quinlan}}</ref><ref name="Vintage Collection" /> His character was created by author [[John Ostrander]] and artist [[Jan Duursema]], though Vos's first non-film appearance was actually a cameo in the [[Timothy Truman]]&ndash;penned [[Star Wars: Emissaries to Malastare|''Emissaries to Malastare'']]. After this, he would take center-stage in the Ostrander/Duursema work [[Star Wars: Twilight|''Twilight'']]. Vos appeared primarily in the ''[[Star Wars: Republic]]'' and [[Star Wars: Jedi (one-shots)|''Star Wars: Jedi'']] comic book series from [[Dark Horse Comics]]. In an interview, Ostrander elaborated on the origins of Quinlan Vos's name, explaining that he patterned after Qui-Gon Jinn; he had wanted a name with the same number of syllables.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.cbr.com/ostrander-uses-the-force-in-vector|text=Ostrander uses the Force in "Vector"|author=Renaud, Jeffrey|date=2008-11-28|work=[https://www.cbr.com Comic Book Resources]|archivedate=20170110015734}}</ref> He was later portrayed by [[Doug Wangler]], a model for Duursema, at [[Celebration III]].<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.sandtroopers.com/events/quinlanvos/interview|text=Interview with Doug Wangler|author=Spice, Chris|date=2006-08-03|work=[http://www.sandtroopers.com sandtroopers.com]|archivedate=20161220032804}}</ref>

Quinlan Vos showed up again in the ''[[Star Wars Tales]]'' comic, "[[Ghost (comic story)|Ghost]]." In the story, Vos rescued a young Han Solo, who was trying to find a treasure with a map he won in [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]], from a swoop gang on Socorro. The swoop gang hunted Vos because they believed him to be a Jedi. After Vos confronted young Solo, he disappeared into the shadows, never to be seen again. However, that ''Star Wars Tales'' issue came out when most of ''Tales'' was considered to be [[Infinities]]. The story is considered, at this point in time, non-canonical in the letters section of [[Star Wars Insider 99|''Star Wars Insider'' 99]].<ref name="Star Wars Insider 99">[[Star Wars Insider 99|''Star Wars Insider'' 99]]</ref>

[[File:Doug_wangler.jpg|thumb|150px|Doug Wangler as Quinlan Vos.]]
[[File:QuinEp3.jpg|thumb|left|290px|Quinlan in an Episode III deleted animatic]]
Intrigued by the character of Vos, [[George Lucas]] included him in the script of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']], but his scene never made it past the animatics stage and was never photographed.<ref name="Trivia">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/hunt-for-ziro-trivia-gallery|text="Hunt for Ziro" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 1}}</ref> However, the character is still mentioned in the final film&mdash;Obi-Wan Kenobi notifies Anakin Skywalker that "Master Vos has moved his troops to Boz Pity."<ref name="Insider85">{{InsiderCite|85|Ask Lobot|Ask the Master}}</ref> According to [[Randy Stradley]], the fate of Vos at the end of the ''Republic'' series came directly from Lucas.<ref name="JCF1">{{JCFCite|url=posts/23104700|board=Literature|thread=Republic #83: The Hidden Enemy, part 3 (of 3)|user=[[Randy Stradley|Randy_Stradley]]|date=2006-02-08|time=11:27 AM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801160614/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/republic-83-the-hidden-enemy-part-3-of-3.21002752/page-5}}</ref> Ostrander had initially considered killing Vos off,<ref name="JCF2">{{JCFCite|url=posts/23122531|board=Literature|thread=Republic #83: The Hidden Enemy, part 3 (of 3)|user=[[John Ostrander|jfostrander]]|date=2006-02-10|time=8:23 AM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801160441/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/republic-83-the-hidden-enemy-part-3-of-3.21002752/page-8}}</ref> and an interview with Duursema in ''Star Wars Insider'' before the final issue's release claimed that he died.

Quinlan Vos and Vilmarh Grahrk action figures were released by [[Hasbro]] in late April 2007 as part of their ''Comic Packs'' line with ''Republic'' #19. Vos was based loosely off of the Siege of Saleucami designs, while Villie's design was straight out of ''Star Wars: Republic'' #19. In 2008 Hasbro released another comic pack with Quinlan Vos and Commander Faie ('08/#13). It also included a reprint of the Star Wars: Republic #82 comic book. Only the upper body of the Quinlan Vos figure is new (new head, arms, and torso).

Quinlan Vos was originally slated to appear in ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode "[[Bombad Jedi]]." He was to be working undercover and actually using his Force abilities to make it look like [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] was a Jedi. He was eventually cut, because at the early stages of production the studio didn't have the ability to include many new characters because of the time it took to create a digital model.<ref name="JCF3">{{JCFCite|url=posts/29630425|board=Star Wars TV|thread=TheForce.Net interviews Henry Gilroy... and Dave Filoni !!! (Your questions answered!)|user=[[Henry Gilroy|HGilroy]]|date=2008-12-30|time=10:34 AM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207114253/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/theforce-net-interviews-henry-gilroy-and-dave-filoni-your-questions-answered.29628723}}</ref> He did eventually make it into the series, appearing in the episode "[[Hunt for Ziro]]." He was voiced by [[Al Rodrigo]].<ref name="SWArchive-''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Hunt for Ziro">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode309.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Hunt for Ziro}}</ref>

After ''The Clone Wars'' was pulled from the air in [[March]] [[2013]], [[Dave Filoni]] and [[Brent Friedman]] indicated that Vos would have been featured alongside Asajj Ventress in a future story arc that never got produced.<ref name="Thank You to TCW Fans">{{SW|url=news/to-fans-of-star-wars-the-clone-wars-thank-you|text=To Fans of ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'': Thank You}}</ref><ref name="Friedman Twitter Vos Arc">{{Twitter|BFree63|status/459356731810643968|[[Brent Friedman]]|quote=@hulitherium @MattMichnovetz Yes. A very dark, very cool one.|archivedate=20190907045717}}</ref><ref name="Friedman Twitter Ventress">{{Twitter|BFree63|status/459437041755766784|[[Brent Friedman]]|quote=@VictorBarnab @hulitherium @MattMichnovetz Yep. Def painful.|archivedate=20190907045713}}</ref> That story arc would later be released as the [[Canon]] novel [[Dark Disciple]].

===Marriage===
Jan Duursema stated the following about Vos and Hentz's marriage:
:''The Kiffar version of marriage is not a ceremony or a legal document. Kiffar 'marriage' is more of a state of mind or a state of being. Through Korto, Khaleen and Quin have an unbreakable connection--and a responsibility that transcends their own separate lives. If you create life, you nurture that life, whatever hardships lie ahead.''<ref name="Marriage" />

{{Noncanonstart|legends=1}}
===The Dark Times===
Vos survived the Clone Wars, but details of his life after that point are sketchy. Around a decade before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], a young [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] encountered an old man matching Quinlan Vos's description on [[Socorro/Legends|Socorro]].<ref name="ghost">{{Tales|11|Ghost (comic story)}}</ref>
{{Noncanonend}}
